sentences.text:
The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in RTA.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner case are that, on 12-08- 2023 at about 7.30 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/JV-0154 along with pillion rider, when they reached near A2B Hotel Service Road, Bhattarahalli, K.R. Pura, Bangalore City stopped his vehicle and waiting for signal, at that time, the driver of one Water Tank bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at a high speed from behind and Tanker wheel ran over the petitioner's left leg.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopedic Hospital and admitted as an inpatient, the petitioner has sustained wound debridement, K-wire fixation of talonavicular joint,
K-wire fixation of medial 4 toes, repair of EHL to EDL, primary closure and bilateral slab.
He underwent surgery for above fracture and internal fixation was done.
Other injuries treated with conservatively, for which he will require huge funds for treatment, medicines etc.,

Accordingly, the petitioner is still under treatment and he was forced to spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses, he required one more surgery for removal of implants in future.
The injuries sustained in the said accident he is completely bed ridden and cannot do his day to day activities.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and he was doing a Quality Checking at Fab Tool Company and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
After the accident, he is unable to do the work and suffering from loss of income.
It is further stated that, the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence driving of driver of the offending Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578.
In this regard, the case was registered at K.R. Puram Traffic Police Station in Cr.No.277/2023 punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
4. On service of notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 entered their appearance through their learned counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

5. Respondent No.1 in its objections has denied all the petition averments and contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts against the company and hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed in limine.
It is admitted the policy issued for the Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578.

Further contended that, the driver of the Tanker was not holding valid and Raj Kumar K vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197359472/
2 effective D.L. as on the date of the accident.

sentences.text: The offending Tanker vehicle was not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident and thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it is contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner alone, who was riding his motorcycle without wearing helmet and without holding valid and effective D.L.

It is further contended that the petitioner managed to file a false complaint before the jurisdictional police against the driver of the Water Tanker and created a false crime records to get compensation.

Respondent No.1 has denied the age,
income and occupation of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Respondent No.2 has contended in his objection that, the allegations made in the petition are false and the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts against him and hence, the petition is liable to be dismissed in limine.
Further, it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has issued a policy in respect of the vehile and it was in force as on the date of accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle was having valid D.L. at the time of accident.
It is further contended that this accident occurred completely negligence of the petitioner and as such the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation.
Respondent No.2 has denied the accident, age, income and occupation of the petitioner.
He has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, he has sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 12-08-2023 at about 7.30 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/JV-0154 along with pillion rider, when they reached near A2B Hotel Service Road, Bhattarahalli,
K.R. Pura, Bangalore City stopped his vehicle and waiting for signal

, at that time, driver of one Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA- 43/3578, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at a high speed from behind and Tanker wheel ran over the petitioner's left leg.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3) What order or award?
8.

REASONS 11. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming the compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
12. The petitioner is examined himself as PW.1 and reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.

16. The respondents have not adduced any evidence and also not produced any documents on their behalf.

17. As per Ex.P.4 spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 sketch and Ex.P.8 charge sheet it appears that, on the date of accident, the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/JV-0154 along with pillion rider, on A2B Hotel Service Road, he stopped his vehicle and waiting for signal, at that time, the driver of Water Tank bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner,
came at a high speed from behind and ran over the petitioner's left leg.
As a result the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Hence, the K.R. Puram Police have filed charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC r/w Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of I.M.V. Act.
18.
Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
For the purpose of disproving the sole negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle, nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
Further, the owner of offending vehicle has not challenged the charge sheet.

19. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
20.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 has took the contention that, the driver of the Lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Respondent No.2 has handed over the possession of the vehicle to the said driver and has contravened the proviso of MV Act and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.

On perusal of Ex.P.9 the copy of notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act and Ex.P.10 reply to the same, it appears that, at the time of accident one Sri. Hari Prasad was driving the offending Tanker Lorry and he has valid licence.
Therefore, it appears that the driver of the offending lorry was hold valid driving licence at the time of accident.

21. Further, respondent No.1 took contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but respondent No.1 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that respondent No.1 has not proved that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

22. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1 the copy of FIR, Ex.P.2 the copy of first information, Ex.P.3 the Police Intimation, Ex.P.4 the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5 the copy of Sketch, Ex.P.6 the IMV Report,
Ex.P.7 the copy of Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 the Charge Sheet, Ex.P.9 the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act and Ex.P.10 the reply to the Notice, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

26. The petitioner contended that, due to injuries he was suffering from pain and mental agony and he is unable to carry on his day to day activities which he used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2.

In the chief-examination affidavit PW.2 deposed that, on 23-10-2024 the Petitioner went to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he has left foot mid-foot amputation and recent X-ray of the left foot shows evidence of mid foot amputation and he was examined clinically,
radiologically and assessment of disability and assessed left foot tarsometatarsal joint amputation 40%.

PW.4 has stated in his chief affidavit that he know the petitioner, who was working as a Junior Quality Engineer in his Company and his monthly salary of Rs.21,555/-, he was met with an Accident on 12/08/2023, after that still he is not attending his duty and hence, the salary was not paid.
Further, PW.4 has produced Ex.P.24 appointment letter, Ex.P.25 resignation letter and Ex.P.26 salary slips for the month of June 2023 to August 2023.

On perusal of the said documents and Bank statement at Ex.P.15, it appears that, the petitioner was working in the FAB Tools Industries Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore and has given resignation to his job and also he was drawing a salary of Rs.21,555/- p.m. till August 2023.

29. As per the say of petitioner, he was working as a Junior Quality Engineer at Fab Tool Company,
Bangalore, he was earning Rs.21,555/- p.m.
To prove the same, he has produced salary slips at Ex.P.26 and also produced Ex.P.15 Bank Statement of Axis Bank.

On perusal of the same, it appears that, the petitioner was working as a Junior Quality Engineer at Fab Tool Company, Bangalore and drawn the salary of Rs.21,555/- for the month of February 2023 to August 2023.
On perusal of Ex.P.15, it appears that, the salary amount has paid to the Bank Account of the petitioner in the month of February 2023 to July 2023.

On perusal of Ex.P.25, it appears that, the petitioner has given his resignation on the ground that, he met with an accident on 13-08-2023 and seriously injured, due to physically challenged he is not able to continued the work.
On perusal of it, it is clear that, the petitioner has given resignation letter to his job stating that, he is not able to work due to his physical condition.
PW.4 the employer has also clearly stated that, the petitioner is not attending for his duty and salary was not paid.
Therefore, it is clear that, due to amputation of the left mid foot, the petitioner is not in a condition to work and therefore, he is not attending his work.
Due to non- attending of the work he has not been paid.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is not in a condition to do his quality checking work as a Junior Quality Engineer due to the injuries sustained in the accident and amputation caused.
The petitioner has forced to resign to his job due to the said accident and injuries.
Therefore, this Tribunal has taken his salary of Rs.21,555/-as his income and considered it for the calculating the loss of future income.

30. In support of age, the petitioner produced notarized copy of his Aadhar Card and his also DL,
which are marked as Ex.P.17 and 18.
As per said documents the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 10-05-2000.
In the wound certificate and discharge summary, the age of the petitioner is shown as 23 years.
This accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, age of the petitioner is considered as 23 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 18 which comes as follows:
Rs.21,555 x 12 x 18 x 35% = Rs.16,29,558/-
Hence, this Tribunal has award Rs.16,29,558/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.

34. Interest:
 In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016(between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the Raj Kumar K vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197359472/
8 rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses) and not more than that.

sentences.text: Hence, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
35. Liability:-
As already observed above, Respondent No.1 is the insurer and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the Water Tanker Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-43/3578.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further the Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
36. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.21,30,286/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.

After deposit, 50% of the compensation amount with accrued interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years and remaining compensation amount with accrued interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 12-08-2023 at about 7.30 p.m. when he was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/JV-0154 along with pillion rider, when they reached near A2B Hotel Service Road, Bhattarahalli,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming the compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
As a result the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, the K.R. Puram Police have filed charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC r/w Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of I.M.V. Act.
18.
Therefore it is clear that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
For the purpose of disproving the sole negligence of the rider of the Motorcycle, nothing has been eliciting from the mouth of the petitioner.
Further, the owner of offending vehicle has not challenged the charge sheet.
19. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
20.
Respondent No.1 has took the contention that, the driver of the Lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Respondent No.2 has handed over the possession of the vehicle to the said driver and has contravened the proviso of MV Act and has committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it appears that the driver of the offending lorry was hold valid driving licence at the time of accident.
There is nothing on record to show that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that respondent No.1 has not proved that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Due to non- attending of the work he has not been paid.

36. Issue No.3:
For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.21,30,286/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.1 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, 50% of the compensation amount with accrued interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years and remaining compensation amount with accrued interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
